one_line: Today's developments include data centre infrastructure plans, regulatory actions on AI agents, and new legal challenges involving OpenAI and copyright law.

themes.title: Data centre expansions and infrastructure talks
themes.text: Japan's JERA is discussing data centre projects with Anthropic and Meta, while Bharti Airtel announced a ₹1,200 crore investment in three Assam facilities. Developers are also proposing vertical data centres to handle high demand and land limits.

stories.headline: Japan's JERA enters talks with Anthropic and Meta to build data centres
Developers propose vertical data centers as Kansas City blocks high-rise plan
Bharti Airtel to invest ₹1,200 crore in three Assam data centres

themes.title: UK regulator targets personal AI agents
themes.text: Following the launch of Meta's Muse personal AI agent in the UK, the Competition and Markets Authority issued guidance requiring user control over data access. Meta subsequently updated its UK terms of service to align with local consumer law.

stories.headline: UK regulator warns AI agents must provide user control as Meta Muse launches
Meta changes UK Muse terms of service to reflect consumer law

themes.title: Legal disputes involve OpenAI and copyright
themes.text: OpenAI filed a trade secrets countersuit against Apple in California. Meanwhile, the Delhi High Court agreed to examine whether an AI system can be recognized as an author under copyright law.

stories.headline: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secrets and supplier threats
Delhi High Court to examine if AI can be author under copyright law
